subject: RPS & token signoff — runbook, owners, and burst lanes
messages:
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@horizonhealth.com>, IT Ops <itops@horizonhealth.com>
Cc: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Nov 2026 15:12:00 -0800
Subject: RPS & token signoff — runbook, owners, and burst lanes

Hi Maya / Horizon team —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap + next steps so we can lock down trial readiness and sign the traffic profile: 

What we covered (short):
- Primary workload: API-driven smart triage for chat summaries and patient intake (mixed generative + reranking).
- Expected steady-state: ~80 RPS during clinic hours (PST) with concurrency up to 220 concurrent connections in our pilot.
- Burst windows: predictable daily bursts ~1100 RPS for 30–90s during appointment start windows; two larger weekly batch bursts (15m) for lab result processing.
- Token profile: mean request token: ~420 tokens; 99th percentile up to ~3,600 when including long context for complex cases.

Action items we need from Horizon to finalize POC scope and SLOs: 
1) Sign off on the attached traffic template with actual RPS by endpoint and expected token distribution (horizon-poc-traffic-template.xlsx).
2) Confirm whether the weekly batch (lab results) can be delayed by up to 10 minutes in case of capacity constraints — helps us configure graceful degradation.
3) Approve the owner lanes: Redwood (serving + monitoring) vs Horizon (ingest shaping + client retries).

Internal owners I’ve suggested: Ben to own load tests and concordant capacity plan; Priyom to validate KV/cache strategy and run quantized baseline.

Please review the attached template and the short runbook draft (redwood-poc-runbook-v1.md) and reply with signoff or changes by EOB Thursday PST. If that works I’ll schedule the load-probe window for next Tuesday.

Best,

Laura Bennett
Sr. Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0197

Attachments: horizon-poc-traffic-template.xlsx (spreadsheet), redwood-poc-runbook-v1.md (text)
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@horizonhealth.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: IT Ops <itops@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Nov 2026 09:03:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RPS & token signoff — runbook, owners, and burst lanes

Laura — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- The steady-state numbers are correct (80 RPS). The 1100 RPS short bursts are what we see when clinics open and multiple intake forms hit the system simultaneously — typically 45–75s.
- The 3,600-token outliers are mostly anonymized full-thread imports; we can cap import size for the pilot if that simplifies things.
- We can accept delaying the weekly batch by up to 5 minutes, not 10. That is a hard constraint because downstream billing jobs expect near-real-time completion.

I filled in the spreadsheet with per-endpoint splits and uploaded it to the shared Drive link in your note. One ask: can Redwood provide a suggested concurrency throttle at the client SDK level so we don’t overwhelm the gateway during bursts?

I’ll mark our tentative signoff on the template pending Ben and Priyom’s feasibility notes.

—Maya
Maya Patel | Senior Engineering Manager, Platform
Horizon Health
maya.patel@horizonhealth.com

From: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, Maya Patel <maya.patel@horizonhealth.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 11:46:00 -0800
Subject: Re: RPS & token signoff — runbook, owners, and burst lanes

Team / Maya — quick feasibility notes and proposed test windows: 

Feasibility blurbs:
- Baseline (80 RPS): trivial on dedicated pilot config.
- Short bursts (1.1k RPS for ~60s): we recommend a continuous-batch probe with a 3x ramp (300 -> 600 -> 1100 RPS) over a 10-minute window to validate autoscaling and KV warming.
- Long-tail tokens (3.6k): these will drive memory/KV usage; Priyom and I propose a capped experiment (75% of long imports) for the pilot and fall back to a truncated import fallback.

Owner lanes (confirming Laura’s slate):
- Redwood (Ben): load probe orchestration, cluster-level SLO verification, and logging hooks to capture tail latency.
- Redwood (Priyom): cache & quantization baseline; memory profile and cold-KV behavior.
- Horizon (Maya): shaping rules & client SDK throttle; acceptance signoff on degradation behavior.

Proposed test schedule (tentative):
- Friday 11/20 09:00–11:00 PST: baseline + ramp probes (non-peak test window).
- Tuesday 11/24 22:00–22:30 PST: short-burst validation (simulate clinic open).
- Wednesday 11/25 03:00–03:20 PST: weekly batch validation (small window to reduce customer impact).

I’ll attach a probe checklist and the small harness script we run for burst simulation after we finalize the template.

Ben Carter
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-burst-probe-checklist.pdf (stub)
From: laura_bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@horizonhealth.com>, ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, priyom_das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:22:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: RPS & token signoff — runbook, owners, and burst lanes

Perfect — thanks Ben and Maya. 

Confirming next steps and owners (finalized):
- Horizon: upload final per-endpoint RPS & token histogram to the Drive link by EOD Friday (Maya).
- Redwood (Ben): schedule baseline + ramp probes, share the probe checklist and harness by EOD Friday.
- Redwood (Priyom): produce quantization & cache baseline report; propose fallback truncation logic by Monday.
- Laura: I’ll assemble the POC acceptance criteria doc (success gates: <10% p95 latency increase under steady-state, <5% error rate during burst probes, graceful degrade for long imports) and circulate to both teams Monday AM.

If there are any blockers to the proposed test times (11/20, 11/24, 11/25), flag them now and we’ll adjust. Otherwise I’ll book the load window and the shared channels.

Thanks — looking forward to getting this into a short, instrumented pilot.

Laura
